title: Texas foreign passport proof of identity for notarial acts
publicBoundary: Public law and public agency guidance only. Do not add private customer facts, private provider tactics, secrets, or internal operating playbooks.
shortAnswer: Texas has a foreign-passport lane when the document relates to a residential real estate transaction. Texas SOS online training says online identification requirements are the same as traditional notarization, while online notarization adds credential analysis and identity proofing.
exactTexasSosTrainingLanguage: If notarizing a document relating to a residential real estate transaction, you may accept an unexpired passport issued by a foreign country as proof of identity.
exactTexasSosOnlineTrainingLanguage: The identification requirements for online notarization are the same as for traditional notarization.

issueBoundaries.ruleUse: The Texas SOS training wording supports accepting an unexpired passport issued by a foreign country as proof of identity in this lane.
Do not assume the residential real estate wording applies. Check current Texas statute and SOS guidance before relying only on a foreign passport.

Apply the same Texas identification baseline, then analyze the extra online notarization identity proofing and credential-analysis procedures. Do not imply a different Texas passport eligibility rule for online notarization unless a current Texas source says so; online notarization adds credential analysis, identity proofing, and record requirements.
